documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six months after the MI. No angina. Does the rehab exercises at home 3 days a week. Bruises easily on the two blood thinners, no real bleeding.
November lipids: LDL in the 70s on atorvastatin 80, good.
Exam: regular, lungs clear, trace edema. Weight in his range.
Labs today. Same list. Cardiology in March. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit 03/20/2025.
CAD s/p RCA DES 08/2024, HFpEF. No angina, no heart failure symptoms beyond his usual stair limit. BP 126/74, HR 62. Euvolemic.
Meds unchanged: aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin 80, metoprolol succinate 25, furosemide 40, empagliflozin 10, amlodipine 5.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
Plan: clopidogrel through August 2025 (12 months), then aspirin alone. Return 6 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Garden in. Neurology last month: hands and legs unchanged, memory about the same.
Vitals as charted. Exam unchanged.
Continue. Clopidogrel end date per cardiology is August. RTC after summer.

events.reason: Acute left-sided weakness and speech difficulty

reports.text: Noncontrast axial images of the head. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Calvarium intact.

Diffusion-weighted images show a small focus of restricted diffusion in the right cerebral hemisphere with matching ADC signal loss, consistent with an acute infarct. No hemorrhage or hemorrhagic transformation. No mass. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.
reports.conclusion: Small acute ischemic infarct, right cerebral hemisphere. No hemorrhage.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 08/03/2025, arrival 09:05, brought by his wife. Stroke alert on arrival.

HPI: 74 yo man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, prior MI and heart failure. At breakfast, about 2 hours before arrival, he suddenly could not use his left side well and had trouble getting words out.
Meds per wife: lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin, glyburide 5 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, albuterol as needed.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol.

Vitals: BP 154/92, pulse 84, RR 16.
Neuro: left lower facial droop with the forehead spared. Left arm and leg weaker than right. Expressive aphasia. 
CT head without contrast: no hemorrhage.

Assessment: acute ischemic stroke within the treatment window, no contraindication identified with the stroke team.
IV alteplase given at 09:40 after BP confirmed under threshold. Admitted to the stroke unit.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, stroke service. Admitted 08/03/2025, discharged 08/06/2025.

Diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, treated with IV alteplase.
Course: no bleeding after thrombolysis. Speech normal by day 2. Left arm and leg strength much improved; mild left hand weakness and clumsiness at discharge. MRI brain 08/04: small acute infarct in the right cerebral hemisphere, no hemorrhage. Continuous telemetry for the stay: sinus rhythm, no atrial fibrillation.
Noted on reconciliation that he was already on aspirin and clopidogrel (12-month course after 2024 RCA stent, about to end).

Discharge plan:
- Aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg together for 90 days from the stroke, then aspirin alone.
- Atorvastatin 80 mg daily.
- Other home medications unchanged.
- Outpatient physical and occupational therapy.
- No driving until cleared.
- Follow up with PCP in 1 week, neurology in 3 months.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

documents.title: Wife calling, stroke
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Wife called. Sunday morning at breakfast Leonard's left side went weak and his words would not come; she called 911. At the regional hospital they gave him the clot-busting medicine. This morning he is talking normally, left hand still clumsy. On the stroke unit, maybe home Wednesday.
Scheduled transitional visit next Tuesday 8/12. Records request faxed.

orders.reason: after ischemic stroke, left hand weakness

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife and son. Discharged 8/6. The ED note came yesterday; no discharge summary yet, so working from the family and the hospital's after-visit sheet.

S: speech back to normal by his and his wife's account. Left hand clumsy with buttons and writing, a little better each day. Walking at his baseline with the cane. No headache, no new weakness, no bleeding.
After-visit sheet: continue aspirin and clopidogrel together for 90 days, atorvastatin 80, therapy, no driving.

O: BP and HR as charted. Speech fluent, naming intact. Face symmetric now. Left grip mildly weaker than right, fine finger movements slower on the left. Leg strength symmetric. Gait spastic as before, steady with cane.

A/P
1. Acute ischemic stroke 8/3, treated with alteplase, mild residual left hand weakness: continue dual antiplatelets 90 days (to early November), then aspirin alone; outpatient PT/OT order sent since the hospital referral had not reached anyone. No driving.
2. CAD, HFpEF: unchanged, keep metoprolol, furosemide, empagliflozin, amlodipine.
3. T2DM, HTN: no changes.
Neurology in 3 months. Here early November.

documents.title: Physical and occupational therapy evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient rehab. Evaluation 08/25/2025.
Dx: recent right hemisphere ischemic stroke; underlying cervical myelopathy.
Findings: mild left hand weakness, slowed fine motor speed on the left. Gait spastic, steady with single point cane. Timed Up and Go 16 s.
Plan: 2x/week for 6 weeks; fine motor training, grip strengthening, balance. Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

documents.title: Discharge summary received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stroke discharge summary finally in, four weeks after discharge. Reviewed: MRI small right hemisphere infarct, telemetry without AF, plan matches what the family told us. Called Mrs. Archambault to let her know nothing changes.

documents.title: Optometry diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated diabetic exam 09/18/2025. No diabetic retinopathy OU. Visual fields by confrontation full. Recall 1 year.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu high-dose L deltoid, updated Pfizer R deltoid. Pressure held 2 minutes each, he is on two antiplatelets. Says therapy finished last week and his hand writes his name neatly again.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Stroke Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months after the stroke. Finished PT/OT. Hand feels normal to him, writing and buttons fine. No new symptoms. Neurology visit 10/30 by son's report: no deficits, stop clopidogrel at 90 days; their letter not here yet.
Exam: speech normal, face symmetric, grip equal, fine finger movements equal. Gait as before his stroke, spastic from the neck, with cane.
A/P
1. Ischemic stroke 8/2025, no residual deficit: stop clopidogrel today, aspirin 81 continues alone. Atorvastatin 80.
2. CAD: stent now 15 months out, aspirin alone is in line with cardiology.
3. Not driving.
Wellness visit next month with fasting labs.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology group. Visit 10/30/2025.
Three months after a right hemisphere ischemic stroke treated with alteplase. Left hand weakness resolved after therapy. Speech normal. Memory stable per family. Myelopathy exam unchanged.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
Plan: stop clopidogrel at 90 days, aspirin 81 alone. Atorvastatin 80. BP and diabetes per PCP. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, wife present.
A hard year: MI follow-up and a stroke in August, now recovered. No falls.
Function: self-care independent, IADLs by wife. Not driving. Son does errands.
PHQ-2 0. Says he is "still here and still stubborn."
Cognition: neurology says stable; family sees no change since the stroke.
Vaccines current. No more colon screening by prior decision.
Advance care plan unchanged, proxy on file.
Labs today. RTC 2 to 3 months.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Quiet winter at home. No chest pain, breathing at baseline, no new neuro symptoms. Weights steady.
Exam unchanged.
BMP today. Continue. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requests 90-day refills: metoprolol succinate 25, furosemide 40, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 80. Last visit 2/10, BMP normal. Sent per protocol.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Doing okay. Sits out on the porch most afternoons. No chest pain, stairs with his usual one rest, no orthopnea. No new weakness or speech trouble. Prostate symptoms steady. Rare albuterol.
Exam: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema. Grip equal. Gait spastic with cane, unchanged.
A/P: CAD, HFpEF, HTN, T2DM, cervical myelopathy, MCI, BPH, history of stroke: all stable. A1c and BMP today. Continue the current list. Front desk to set up a fall visit when the schedule opens.

documents.title: Labs from Friday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leonard and family, Friday's labs look fine: A1c in your usual range, kidney function and potassium steady. No changes. Enjoy the summer.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request for metformin 1000 mg, glyburide 5 mg and empagliflozin 10 mg, 90 days. A1c 6/19 reviewed. Sent.

events.reason: Sudden vertigo, nausea and trouble walking

reports.text: Noncontrast axial images. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect. Posterior fossa structures without acute abnormality on CT. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 08/02/2026, arrival 11:20, brought by wife.

CC: dizziness, nausea, unable to walk straight.
HPI: 75 yo man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes for about 30 years, hyperlipidemia, asthma, and an ischemic stroke in 2025. Four hours ago he suddenly felt the room spin, became nauseated and has vomited twice. Cannot walk without veering.
Meds per wife: lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin, metformin, glyburide, daily multivitamin, albuterol HFA as needed.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
SH: never smoker, 1-2 drinks a month, retired accountant.
FH: father MI at 61, mother type 2 diabetes, brother ischemic stroke at 65.

Exam: horizontal nystagmus, worse looking to the right. Mild right Horner syndrome. Right arm and leg ataxia with dysmetria on finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin. Strength full, sensation intact. Speech mildly slurred. Veers to the right on attempted gait.
CT head without contrast: no hemorrhage.

Impression: acute ischemic stroke, posterior circulation, right-sided findings.
Plan: stroke neurology consulted at bedside. Admitted to the stroke unit for MRI and further care.

documents.title: Dad was in the hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, Marc here. Dad was admitted on Aug 2 with bad dizziness and they said another stroke, in the back of the brain this time. He came home Friday. He is walking with the cane and Mom is with him. They told us to follow up with you. What should we do?

documents.title: RE: Dad was in the hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Marc, thank you for letting us know, and I am sorry. We have not received anything from the hospital yet and I have asked for the records. Please call the front desk tomorrow to book a hospital follow-up in the next week or two, and bring all of his medicine bottles and the discharge papers. If he has new weakness, trouble speaking, worse dizziness or a fall, call 911.
